title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Pricing a Block Multiple by Multiple
content:
**Basis 1.** Where the multiples sold stand at or above 4 and unexpired blocks already stand on the
program, the block is priced multiple by multiple, the first multiple at the tier's block hour rate and
each further multiple at the rate the block steps to.

**Basis 2.** Where two or three multiples are sold, the whole block is priced at the rate the block
steps to.

**Basis 3.** In any other case neither basis above changes how the block is priced.

The hours sold are the multiples sold multiplied by the minimum purchase published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs. Blocks standing
unexpired on the program are those bought within the tier's expiry period:

| Program | Expiry period (calendar months) | Minimum purchase (hours) |
|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 0 | 0 |
| Priority Response Program | 0 | 0 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 12 | 40 |
| Emergency Response Program | 12 | 40 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 18 | 60 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 24 | 100 |

| The multiples sold | Unexpired blocks already standing on the program | The basis |
|---|---|---|
| 4 or more | some stand | the first multiple at the tier's block hour rate, each further multiple at the rate the block steps to |
| 4 or more | none stands | neither basis above changes how the block is priced |
| two or three | any | the whole block at the rate the block steps to |
| one | any | neither basis above changes how the block is priced |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** On a program whose minimum purchase is 40 hours, 5 multiples sold where
unexpired blocks already stand price 40 hours at the tier's block hour rate and the remaining 160 hours
at the rate the block steps to; the same 5 multiples on a program carrying no unexpired block are not
priced multiple by multiple. Three multiples price all 120 hours at the rate the block steps to.
